blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Self-Improvement Loop**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Curation, § The Self-Improvement Loop
blocks.md: Suppose a curation round for the connection-pool repair agent retains only straight-line, clean executions while discarding messier traces where the agent recovers from misleading test diagnostics. Fine-tuning on that corpus strengthens straightforward repairs while leaving recovery unimproved, and in the next round a higher nominal pass rate hides that gap rather than closing it.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Rejection-sampling fine-tuning
- Staleness and coverage narrowing
- Production feedback signals

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Learning artifacts from one record matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: One recorded run can yield imitation material, a preference comparison, or a rollout fixture, and each use has its own admission conditions rather than inheriting the run's outcome.

questions.q: The section **The Self-Improvement Loop** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A trajectory class has different shares by records, processed tokens, and selected target tokens, so a mixture is specified in targets and budgeted in processed tokens.
With k attempts per task a random trace split puts most tasks on both sides, so partitions are assigned to task groups that hold every attempt, paraphrase, fork, and derived record.
One recorded run can yield imitation material, a preference comparison, or a rollout fixture, and each use has its own admission conditions rather than inheriting the run's outcome.
A generate-select-train loop carries contrast only on informative tasks, so it narrows toward what it already solves, and hard and trivial fixtures cost attempts without teaching.
